text.p: A newspaper poll shows the popularity of Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's administration has dropped, but approval of the government's anti-inflation Real Plan remains stable.
The Folha de Sao Paulo survey found that only 39 percent of those interviewed considered Cardoso's government to be excellent or good, as opposed to 42 percent in May.
But, 74 percent of respondents approved of the Real Plan, virtually unchanged from May's 76-percent approval rating. Seventeen percent said the plan was bad.
The poll showed 42 percent of those interviewed said the government's performance was average, 16 percent said it was bad and the rest had no opinion.

Folha de Sao Paulo said the government's approval rating has been falling since the end of last year when it reached its peak, while approval for the Real Plan had remained stable over the same period.

The government's approval rating of 47 percent in December started to fall in the new year with the introduction of credit restrictions to clamp down on consumption, the privatization of mining giant CVRD and news of a cash-for-votes scandal, Folha said.
In December, 76 percent thought the Real Plan was good, only slightly more than now.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
